intent: Trace the share of African Americans living in the South over the period from 1950 to 2010 to identify the direction and turning points in that share.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
What is the direction and what are the turning points in the share of African Americans living in the South from 1950 to 2010?

units.claim: All 1 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: The share of African Americans living in the South declined from 0.92 in 1950 to a minimum of 0.26 in 1990, then rose to 0.51 in 2010, so the trend reverses direction around 1990.
units.computation: Compare successive values: 0.92 (1950) > 0.31 (1970) > 0.26 (1990), then 0.26 (1990) < 0.51 (2010); the minimum occurs at 1990, marking the turning point from decline to increase.
accept: Share declines from 1950 to 1990 and then increases to 2010.
The lowest share is in 1990, and the direction reverses after 1990.
Values go from 0.92 in 1950 down to 0.26 in 1990 and back up to 0.51 in 2010.
reject: The share increases continuously from 1950 to 2010.
The share declines continuously from 1950 to 2010.
The turning point is in 1970 or 2010 rather than 1990.

optional_valid: Mentioning the absolute decline from 0.92 to 0.26 between 1950 and 1990.
Mentioning the absolute increase from 0.26 to 0.51 between 1990 and 2010.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal explanations for the decline or reversal.
Claims about data points not present in the table summary.
Comparing this panel to another panel, since there is only one panel.
review_notes: The intent asks for direction and turning points, so a single trend unit covering the full 1950-2010 sequence with the 1990 minimum is sufficient.
Only the four anchor rows supplied in the table summary are used as basis rows.
